title: React Fundamentals
description: Components, props, state and hooks in modern React

questions.question: What syntax extension lets you write HTML-like markup inside JavaScript in React?
questions.explanation: JSX looks like HTML but compiles to JavaScript function calls that create React elements.

questions.question: Which hook adds local state to a function component?
questions.explanation: useState returns the current value and a setter. Calling the setter schedules a re-render with the new value.

questions.question: How does data normally flow between React components?
questions.explanation: React uses one-way data flow: parents pass props down. Children talk back by calling functions the parent passed in.

questions.question: Why does React need a 'key' prop on items rendered from a list?
questions.explanation: Keys let React match list items across renders so it can update, reorder or remove the right elements. Stable IDs work best.

questions.question: When does a useEffect with an empty dependency array ([]) run?
questions.explanation: With [] the effect runs once after the component mounts, and its cleanup runs when it unmounts. (Strict Mode runs it twice in development to surface bugs.)

questions.question: What should you do instead of mutating state directly, e.g. `state.items.push(x)`?
choices: Call the setter with a new array or object
questions.explanation: React detects changes by reference. Create a new value, such as setItems([...items, x]), so React knows to re-render.

questions.question: Which hook lets a component read a value without passing props through every level?
questions.explanation: useContext reads the nearest Provider's value, which avoids 'prop drilling' through intermediate components.

questions.question: What does a React component return to describe its UI?
questions.explanation: Components return React elements, usually written as JSX. React works out the DOM changes needed to match them.

questions.question: Which hook holds a mutable value that persists across renders without triggering a re-render?
questions.explanation: useRef returns an object whose .current property survives re-renders. Changing it does not cause a re-render.

questions.question: What is the rule about where hooks can be called?
choices: At the top level of components or custom hooks
questions.explanation: Hooks must be called in the same order every render, so they belong at the top level, not inside conditions, loops or nested functions.
